400.description: The request is refused: a label written twice, a label the pool does not carry, or a life longer than a day. A request carrying two credentials is refused as well.

403.description: The caller is not an administrator, or holds a session that may only enrol.

404.description: No runner pool of that name: the caller is an administrator already, so this names the pool rather than hiding the route.

bearer.description: An API token in the Authorization header, as agk, the mobile applications, the Terraform provider and every script present one: minted at POST /api/v1/auth/tokens or by agk login's exchange, stored as its SHA-256, shown once, expiring after 90 days unless asked otherwise and after a year at most, its use recorded at every request. Until the first administrator has signed in, at their first passkey or at the first request of a full session their password opens, the bootstrap token, AGENTIIK_OPERATOR_TOKEN, is presented the same way, as the principal operator; it is refused from then on, and its hash forgotten. A bearer token sets, changes and removes no credential, a passkey, a password or a TOTP generator, since a token that leaked would otherwise be a way to a credential that outlives it. A request carrying one beside a session cookie is refused with 400.

session.name: __Host-agentiik_session
session.description: The browser's session, opened by a sign-in on the sign-in page: 256 bits in the cookie __Host-agentiik_session, HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, Path=/, no Domain and no expiry of its own, kept by the server as its SHA-256 and revocable there. The __Host- prefix makes a browser refuse the cookie unless it is Secure, set for the whole origin and bound to no Domain, so no other host under the same domain can set it. It ends 12 hours after its last request, 30 days after it opened however it is used, at POST /api/v1/auth/sign-out, and with its user or the credential that opened it, and opens nothing while its user is suspended. A GET, a HEAD or an OPTIONS carrying it is answered from whatever page, since SameSite=Lax lets a link followed from another site carry the cookie and the API answers no cross-origin read; any other method is answered only where its one Origin header is the public URL's origin, and 403 otherwise, before the session is looked up, since SameSite=Lax counts a page of another host of the same site as the same site. It records the credential that opened it, so that what it may do is read at every request from that credential and the policy that applies then, rather than kept by convention: a password's, where the policy requires a passkey, registers passkeys, sets its password and signs out, and answers 403 everywhere else; a password's where passwords are now forbidden, and a synced passkey's where device_bound_only now applies, open nothing. A request carrying it beside a bearer token, or carrying two of it, is refused with 400.

error.title: Error
error.description: A refusal: one sentence saying what was refused, and, where a setting of the authentication policy is the reason, that setting's name. It says nothing a caller could not already know, which is why a namespace or a workflow the caller cannot see is refused with the same sentence as one that does not exist. The same shape as every refusal the API already answers.
What was refused, in one sentence meant for the person reading it. A client shows it and matches nothing against it: the status is what a program branches on.
examples: no such thing, or not yours
you do not hold what this needs
removing this passkey would leave fewer than min_passkeys

setting.description: The setting of the authentication policy the refusal is about, spelled as the policy spells it: a setting a namespace's policy would loosen; password where passwords are forbidden, where an installation addressed by an IP address cannot forbid them, or where a change would leave no administrator able to sign in; device_bound_only for a synced passkey, or for such a change; min_passkeys for a removal it forbids; passkey for a password that could only ever open a session that enrols. Absent where no setting is the reason. Left a string rather than an enumeration here, because the policy's own keys are the list and a copy of it would drift.

examples.error: no such thing, or not yours
a namespace may tighten the installation's policy, never loosen it: device_bound_only is true there

base64url.title: Base64url
base64url.description: Bytes written base64url without padding, the Base64URLString Web Authentication's JSON forms use for every binary member, so that what the browser's toJSON() and parseCreationOptionsFromJSON() read and write travels unchanged.

ceremony.title: Ceremony
ceremony.description: Which of the two passkey ceremonies a request belongs to: registration records a new passkey for a user, assertion signs a user in with one they hold. The words are Web Authentication's own.

liveChange.title: Live change
liveChange.description: One message of the live connection, GET /api/v1/me/live: what changed, named and never held.

kind.description: What changed: a run, or one of its steps or tasks; the caller's notifications; the runners or their pools; to an administrator, a run anywhere, named nowhere, which GET /api/v1/stats/activity counts; or anything, where a change may have been missed.

namespace.description: The namespace of the run, for a run alone.

workflow.description: The workflow of the run, for a run alone.

run.description: The run, for a run alone.

sessionKind.title: Session kind
sessionKind.description: What a session may do, as it was when it opened; what it may do is read again from the policy at every request. full reaches every route the principal's grants allow. enrolment is a session a password opened where the policy that applies to the account requires a passkey, whatever passkeys it holds: it registers passkeys, sets the password that opened it and signs out, and nothing else, so it cannot read a workflow, start a run or mint a token. The server records the credential that opened each session, so the difference is known to it rather than kept by convention.

apiTokenValue.title: API token value
apiTokenValue.description: The clear value of an API token, shown once in the answer that mints it and never again, since only its hash is kept. agktoken_ and at least 43 base64url characters, which is 256 bits: the prefix says what the value is before anybody tries it, as agkjoin_ and agkrunner_ do on the wire, so one that leaks into a log can be recognised and revoked by whoever finds it.

enrolmentCode.title: Enrolment code
enrolmentCode.description: A single-use code authorising the enrolment of a passkey, or of a password where the policy allows passwords, for one user and nothing else, good for an hour: the code a first administrator's link or a new user's link carries after #, and a recovery code. One kind of value for the three, because each authorises the same thing and is audited as the same action, enrolment.issue. 256 bits, stored hashed, with a prefix so that one found in a chat or a ticket is recognised for what it is.

exchangeCode.title: Exchange code
exchangeCode.description: The one-time code the sign-in page sends the browser back to agk login's loopback address with: single use, good for a minute, and worth nothing without the verifier whose SHA-256 opened the page.

codeChallenge.title: Code challenge
codeChallenge.description: The SHA-256 of agk login's one-time verifier, base64url without padding, as RFC 7636 computes S256: 43 characters. The only method there is, so no method is named: a verifier sent in the clear would be a code anyone on the way could complete.

codeVerifier.title: Code verifier
codeVerifier.description: agk login's one-time verifier, as RFC 7636 writes one: 43 to 128 unreserved characters. It never leaves agk until the exchange, which is what makes a code seen on the way worthless.

loopbackUri.title: Loopback address
loopbackUri.description: Where agk login listens: plain http on a port of the loopback interface, by address and never by the name localhost, as RFC 8252 advises for a native application's redirect, since a name can be resolved elsewhere and an address cannot. Nothing else is accepted, so the sign-in page can never be made to hand a code to another host.

terminalSignIn.title: Terminal sign-in
terminalSignIn.description: What agk login handed the sign-in page, passed on by the page with the sign-in it completes, so that the answer sends the browser back to agk with a one-time code. The two travel together: a loopback address without a challenge would be a code anybody on the machine could redeem.

redirect_uri.description: The loopback address agk login listens on, as the sign-in page was opened with it.

code_challenge.description: The SHA-256 of agk login's verifier, as the sign-in page was opened with it. The exchange holds the verifier to it.

PublicKeyCredentialDescriptorJSON.title: PublicKeyCredentialDescriptorJSON
PublicKeyCredentialDescriptorJSON.description: Web Authentication's PublicKeyCredentialDescriptorJSON: one credential, named so that an authenticator can recognise it. Spelled as the Recommendation spells it, and left open, because it is the browser's dictionary and a member it adds is one this document does not own.

type.description: Always public-key, the one credential type Web Authentication defines.

id.description: The credential ID, as the credentials list names the passkey.

transports.description: How the authenticator holding it was reached, a hint for the browser that the Recommendation defines. The API keeps no transports and writes none: a browser finds the authenticator without them.

PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptionsJSON.title: PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptionsJSON
PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptionsJSON.description: Web Authentication Level 3's PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptionsJSON, what PublicKeyCredential.parseCreationOptionsFromJSON() takes to start a registration. Spelled as the Recommendation spells it, camel case included, because the browser reads it and an identifier is never translated; left open, because a member a later browser reads is not this document's to refuse. The members listed are the ones the API sets.

id.description: The Relying Party Identifier, a domain and never an IP address, which a browser refuses.

name.description: What the authenticator shows the person as the site the passkey is for.

rp.description: The Relying Party: the installation, named by the host of AGK_PUBLIC_URL, or of AGK_PROXY_URL behind a proxy, which is the origin the browser checks the page against.

id.description: The user handle, random bytes the API minted for the account, which an assertion hands back as userHandle.

name.description: The login, which the authenticator shows to tell accounts apart.

displayName.description: The display name, shown beside the login.

user.description: The user being enrolled. Its id is a user handle the API minted, never the login, because Web Authentication asks that the handle carry nothing that identifies the person.

challenge.description: A fresh random challenge, single use, which the attestation must sign over.

pubKeyCredParams.description: The key types the API verifies, in order of preference: ES256 (-7), EdDSA (-8) and RS256 (-257), the three COSE algorithms it checks with the Go standard library.

timeout.description: How long, in milliseconds, the ceremony may take before the challenge is abandoned.

excludeCredentials.description: The passkeys the user already holds, by credential ID alone, so that an authenticator does not register a second one for the same account.

residentKey.description: Always required: the passkey is discoverable, which is what lets an assertion start without naming the user.

requireResidentKey.description: true, the Level 1 spelling of the same request, for authenticators that read only that.

userVerification.description: The policy's user_verification: required makes the passkey two factors, the authenticator and whatever unlocks it.

authenticatorSelection.description: What is asked of the authenticator: a discoverable credential, so that signing in needs no login typed first, and the user verification the policy imposes.

attestation.description: Always none. Attestation would certify the authenticator's make, and the synced passkeys most people hold carry none, so asking for it would refuse them or prove nothing.

PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptionsJSON.title: PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptionsJSON
PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptionsJSON.description: Web Authentication Level 3's PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptionsJSON, what PublicKeyCredential.parseRequestOptionsFromJSON() takes to start a sign-in. Spelled as the Recommendation spells it and left open, as its creation counterpart is.

challenge.description: A fresh random challenge, single use, which the assertion must sign.

timeout.description: How long, in milliseconds, the ceremony may take.

rpId.description: The Relying Party Identifier, the host of AGK_PUBLIC_URL or of AGK_PROXY_URL behind a proxy.

allowCredentials.description: Always empty: the authenticator offers whichever passkey it holds for this Relying Party, so no login is sent before the ceremony and none can be probed for.

RegistrationResponseJSON.title: RegistrationResponseJSON
RegistrationResponseJSON.description: Web Authentication Level 3's RegistrationResponseJSON, what PublicKeyCredential.toJSON() returns after navigator.credentials.create(). Sent as the browser serialised it: spelled as the Recommendation spells it and left open, the one object in a request body here that is, because refusing a member a newer browser adds would refuse the browser.

rawId.description: The same ID, which Web Authentication carries twice; the API holds the two to each other.

clientDataJSON.description: The client data the browser assembled: the type webauthn.create, the challenge and the origin, which the API holds to the options it issued and to its own origin.

authenticatorData.description: The authenticator data, also inside the attestation object, where the API reads it: the Relying Party's hash, the flags, Backup Eligibility and Backup State among them, and the new credential's key.

transports.description: How the authenticator was reached, as the browser reports it. Not read: the API keeps no transports.

publicKey.description: The new public key as SubjectPublicKeyInfo, a convenience the browser adds. Not read: the key recorded is the one in the attestation object.

publicKeyAlgorithm.description: The COSE algorithm of the new key, a convenience the browser adds. Not read, for the same reason.

attestationObject.description: The attestation object in CBOR: the format, none being the one the API asks for, and the authenticator data. Decoded by the API's own CBOR decoder, which refuses indefinite lengths, duplicate map keys and trailing bytes.

response.description: The authenticator's attestation response. The API reads clientDataJSON and attestationObject, and decodes the key from the attestation object itself rather than trusting the conveniences beside it.

authenticatorAttachment.description: platform for an authenticator built into the device, cross-platform for one reached over USB, NFC or a phone. Informative only.

clientExtensionResults.description: The results of any extension the browser ran. The API asks for none, and reads nothing here.

AuthenticationResponseJSON.title: AuthenticationResponseJSON
AuthenticationResponseJSON.description: Web Authentication Level 3's AuthenticationResponseJSON, what PublicKeyCredential.toJSON() returns after navigator.credentials.get(). Sent as the browser serialised it, spelled as the Recommendation spells it and left open, as the registration response is.

id.description: The ID of the passkey that signed, which names the account.

clientDataJSON.description: The client data: the type webauthn.get, the challenge and the origin, held to the options issued and to the API's own origin.

authenticatorData.description: The authenticator data: the Relying Party's hash, the flags, user verification and Backup State among them, and the signature counter.

signature.description: The signature over the authenticator data and the hash of the client data, checked with the key the passkey was registered with.

userHandle.description: The user handle the passkey was registered under, which a discoverable credential hands back. Required: the options list no credential, so an assertion names its account by it alone, and it has to be the one that account's passkeys were registered under.

authenticatorAttachment.description: platform or cross-platform, as for a registration. Informative only.

clientExtensionResults.description: The results of any extension the browser ran. Nothing here is read.

passkeyOptionsRequest.title: Passkey options request
passkeyOptionsRequest.description: Which ceremony to start. An assertion names nobody, since the passkey the authenticator offers names the account. A registration is for the account an enrolment code was issued for where one is given, whoever last signed in in that browser, and otherwise for the caller's own account, from its browser session.

ceremony.description: registration to record a new passkey, assertion to sign in with one.

code.description: The code of an enrolment link or a recovery code, for a registration by someone who has no session: the enrolment page reads it from after the # of its own address, which a browser never sends, and hands it here. It is held against the challenge and consumed by the verification that records the passkey, so a ceremony dismissed halfway does not burn it. Refused beside an assertion.

passkeyOptions.title: Passkey options
passkeyOptions.description: The options of the ceremony started, for the page to hand to the browser as they are.

ceremony.description: The ceremony these options start, as asked.

options.description: Web Authentication's own options: PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptionsJSON for a registration, PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptionsJSON for an assertion.

passkeyVerifyRequest.title: Passkey verification request
passkeyVerifyRequest.description: The browser's answer to the options, and what the page adds to it: a label for a new passkey, and agk login's loopback address and challenge for a sign-in it started.

ceremony.description: The ceremony being finished, the same as the options were asked for.

credential.description: What PublicKeyCredential.toJSON() returned: a RegistrationResponseJSON for a registration, an AuthenticationResponseJSON for an assertion.

label.description: A name for the new passkey, so that two on two devices can be told apart when one is lost: at most 256 characters on one line. Registration only.

terminal.description: What agk login opened the sign-in page with, where it did. Assertion only, a registration carrying it being a 400: the answer then carries the loopback address to send the browser to.

redirectTo.title: Redirect to agk login
redirectTo.description: Where the sign-in page sends the browser once a sign-in agk login started has succeeded: the loopback address agk login gave, with the one-time code as its code query parameter, which agk then trades at POST /api/v1/auth/exchange. The API writes the whole address rather than the page assembling it, so that the page can never be made to send a code anywhere the API did not check.

passkeyVerified.title: Passkey verified
passkeyVerified.description: What a verified ceremony did. A registration answers the passkey it recorded. An assertion answers who signed in, the session itself being the cookie set beside it, and, for a sign-in agk login started, where to send the browser next.

login.description: The account the ceremony was for: the one that enrolled, or the one that signed in.

credential.description: The passkey recorded, as the credentials list will show it, kind and flags included. Registration only.

redirect_to.description: Where the page sends the browser next. Present only for an assertion that carried terminal.

passwordLoginRequest.title: Password sign-in request
passwordLoginRequest.description: A login and a password, the fallback an installation can forbid, with a TOTP code where the account holds a generator.

password.description: The password, compared with its Argon2id hash as the bytes sent, and never stored or logged as sent.

totp.description: The current code of the account's TOTP generator, required where the account holds one and refused where it does not. A TOTP exists only alongside a password.

terminal.description: What agk login opened the sign-in page with, where it did: the way agk login signs in on an installation addressed by an IP address, where no passkey can be used.

signIn.title: Signed in
signIn.description: Who signed in with a password and what the session opened may do when it opened. The session itself is the cookie set beside this answer.

session.description: full, or enrolment where the policy that applies to the account requires a passkey, whatever passkeys it holds.

redirect_to.description: Where the page sends the browser next, for a sign-in agk login started. Never beside a session that may only enrol, which mints no token.

exchangeRequest.title: Code exchange request
exchangeRequest.description: agk login's code and verifier, the two halves of PKCE, named as RFC 7636 names them.

code.description: The code the browser brought back to the loopback address.

code_verifier.description: The verifier whose SHA-256 opened the sign-in page.

device_label.description: What the token is for, shown when tokens are listed: agk writes agk on and the machine's name, or the label it was asked for.

issuedToken.title: Issued token
issuedToken.description: A token just minted: its value, this once, and its record as the list will show it without the value from now on.

token.description: The clear value, for the Authorization header. Shown here and nowhere else, ever: lose it and mint another.

api_token.description: The token's record: its identifier, which revoking it names, its principal, label, scope and expiry.

me.title: Me
me.description: Who the caller is and what it may do at this moment: its principal, the record behind it, its groups, its effective permissions, and its notifications. The permissions are what the grants resolve to now, the principal's own and its groups', at both scopes, with every deny subtracted, and narrowed by the presenting token's scope where it has one, so that a client hides what the caller does not hold rather than disabling it.

principal.description: The caller as a grant and the audit log write it: a login, or NS/NAME for a service account; operator for the bootstrap token until the first administrator has signed in.

admin.description: Whether the caller administers the installation through the credential it presented: a user created with admin, or the bootstrap token until the first administrator has signed in. It grants no run:read_data anywhere. An administrator's powers pass through a token only where its scope does not narrow them away, so this is false for a token carrying within, which names namespaces and workflows while administering is the installation's, or permissions, which keeps only what it names while administering is none of the nine.

user.description: The caller's account, where the caller is a user: suspended_for among it where the policy suspended it.

examples.title: Technical lead
examples.bio: Writes the invoicing workflows, and reviews what touches payroll.

service_account.description: The caller's record, where the caller is a service account.

groups.description: The groups the caller belongs to, as a grant names them. Empty for a service account, which belongs to a namespace rather than to a team.

permissions.description: The caller's effective permissions, keyed by scope as a grant writes it, narrowed by the presenting token's scope. A namespace's key holds what applies to every workflow in it; a workflow's key, NS/NAME, appears where a grant, a deny or the token's scope makes what applies there other than its namespace's, and holds the whole of it. A namespace the caller holds nothing in is absent, and so is a workflow where the caller holds nothing: it is one the caller cannot read, whose existence no answer names to them, though a client then reads the namespace's permissions as applying there, a convenience that does not outweigh it.

notifications.description: What the installation has to tell the caller, newest first: an administrator having written a grant in a namespace the caller owns by the installation's power, put a user in a group holding a role there, or widened their own access there, each with the act and who did it, told to the other administrators too where the namespace had nobody to tell; a sign-in refused for one of the caller's passkeys' signature counters; and a recovery code agentiik-api recover issued an administrator, told to every administrator. Each is kept 90 days from when it was written, or until the caller dismisses it with DELETE /api/v1/me/notifications/{id}; one past its days is removed as this is read. Empty through a token narrowed by a scope, which reads none.

user.title: Technical lead
user.bio: Writes the invoicing workflows, and reviews what touches payroll.

credentialList.title: Credential list
credentialList.description: The caller's credentials, each described and none held: no public key, no hash, no shared secret.

credentials.description: Passkeys, the password where one is still stored, and a TOTP generator where one is enrolled, oldest first. Empty for a service account, which holds tokens only, and for the bootstrap token.

tokenRequest.title: Token request
tokenRequest.description: What to mint. Every member is optional: an empty object mints a token for the caller, expiring in 90 days, with the caller's full rights.

principal.description: Whose token it is: the caller's own login, or a service account of a namespace the caller owns, written NS/NAME. Absent means the caller, and written empty is refused. Never a group, which holds no credential, and never a namespace's built-in NS/agentiik, for which none is minted.

device_label.description: What the token is minted on or for, so that a list of tokens can be read and the one on a lost machine revoked: at most 256 characters, and absent rather than empty where there is none.

expires_at.description: When the token stops being accepted. Absent means 90 days from now. Already past, or later than a year from now, is refused, a minute past the year taken as asked for a client whose clock runs a little ahead: no token is a credential for good, and every one is renewed by someone who still means it.

scope.description: What the token is narrowed to: permissions it keeps and the namespaces and workflows it reaches. It can only narrow: the token's rights are its principal's intersected with it.

tokenList.title: Token list
tokenList.description: API tokens as they are listed: never a value.

tokens.description: The caller's tokens and those of the service accounts of namespaces it owns that are still accepted, newest first; an expired or revoked token is gone from the list. Through a token narrowed by a scope, that token alone.

namespaceCreate.title: Namespace creation
namespaceCreate.description: A shared namespace to create: its name and, where an administrator creates it, its owner and its quotas. The record answered is the one GET /api/v1/namespaces lists.

name.description: The namespace's name, the first path segment of its routes. Refused where a namespace holds it, as its name or a former one, or a login does.

kind.description: Always shared, and shared where it is left out. A personal namespace is created at its user's first sign-in, named after their login, and never here: personal is refused.

owner.description: Who owns it: a user or group:NAME, given the owner role on the namespace in the same transaction, so that it can share the namespace and act in it from the start. Left out, the caller owns it, which the bootstrap token, being nobody, cannot. Naming another owner than the caller is an administrator's. The owner is who is told when an administrator writes a grant there by the installation's power or widens their own access in it.

quotas.description: What it may consume, an administrator's to write. max_concurrent_tasks starts at 20 where left out, and the other five bound nothing until set; PUT /api/v1/namespaces/{ns}/quotas changes them later, an administrator's as well.

namespaceUpdate.title: Namespace settings
namespaceUpdate.description: What PATCH /api/v1/namespaces/{ns} changes, as a partial object: each field named is set and each left out kept, null refused rather than read as either. It is the namespace's settings and takes more fields as they grow, each written by whoever holds grant:manage at the namespace's scope or administers the installation. The quotas are not among them: they are an administrator's alone, at PUT /api/v1/namespaces/{ns}/quotas.

name.description: The namespace's new name, on the grammar every namespace's name is written on. The name it leaves becomes a former name, still the namespace's; a name a namespace, a login or a reserved word holds, or a former name of another namespace, is refused.

namespaceList.title: Namespace list
namespaceList.description: Namespaces as the caller may see them.

namespaces.description: The namespaces the caller holds a grant in, directly or through a group, or every one for an administrator; its personal namespace among them. By name.

userCreate.title: User creation
userCreate.description: A user to create, as agk user create sends it: what it was given and nothing more, so that the same command run again asks for the same user. The display name is not among it: it is made of the given and family names.

login.description: What the user signs in as, and the name of the personal namespace created on their first sign-in. Refused where a namespace or another user holds it.

given_name.description: The name the user is called by, which with the family name makes the name people read. Left out, a user created has none, and is shown by their login while they say neither name, and a user asked for again keeps what is recorded. The user writes it once signed in.

family_name.description: The user's family name, the second half of the name people read. Left out, a user created has none, and a user asked for again keeps what is recorded. The user writes it once signed in.

email.description: An address for the people the user works with to reach them at, which nothing sends anything to. Left out, a user created has none, and a user asked for again keeps what is recorded. An administrator changes it later at PATCH /api/v1/users/{login}.

admin.description: true for a platform administrator, as agk user create --admin asks. Left out, a user created is not one, and a user asked for again keeps what is recorded.

userUpdate.title: User change
userUpdate.description: What an administrator changes of a user after creating them, and nothing else: the email address, set to what the field holds, the empty string removing it, and kept where it is left out. Null is refused rather than read as either. The names and the rest of the profile are the user's, and the display name nobody's.

email.description: The address the people the user works with reach them at, which nothing sends anything to; the empty string removes it.

enrolmentLink.title: Enrolment link
enrolmentLink.description: A link that enrols the first credential of an account holding none, a passkey, or a password where the policy allows passwords: single use, good for an hour, shown once and stored hashed.

link.description: The enrolment page on the Relying Party's origin, with the code after #. A browser never sends what follows #, so the code reaches no access log, a proxy's included.

expires_at.description: When the link stops working, an hour after it was issued.

createdUser.title: Created user
createdUser.description: The user created, or asked for again, and the link that enrols their first credential.

user.description: The account, as GET /api/v1/users lists it.

enrolment.description: The enrolment link, shown this once.

recoveryCode.title: Recovery code
recoveryCode.description: A recovery code for a user who lost what signs them in, as a code to read out or type and as a link to the enrolment page carrying it. Single use, good for an hour, authorising the enrolment of a passkey, or of a password where the policy allows passwords, and nothing else, and never sent by mail, which would put the account back behind a mailbox.

code.description: The code, which the enrolment page takes typed.

link.description: The enrolment page with the code after #, for an administrator handing it over as a link.

expires_at.description: When the code stops working, an hour after it was issued.

users.description: Every user, by login, with no credential in any of them.

groupCreate.title: Group creation
groupCreate.description: A group to create, empty or with its first members.

name.description: The group's name, written after group: wherever a principal is expected. Refused where a group already holds it.

members.description: Its first members, by login, up to 1,024 of them. Absent creates it empty; members are added one by one after that.

groups.description: Every group, by name, with its members.

serviceAccountCreate.title: Service account creation
serviceAccountCreate.description: A service account to create in a namespace the caller owns, written NS/NAME from then on.

namespace.description: The namespace it belongs to, one the caller owns.

name.description: Its name within the namespace. agentiik is refused: it is the built-in identity's name in every namespace and no other's.

serviceAccountList.title: Service account list
serviceAccountList.description: Service accounts as the caller may see them.

service_accounts.description: The service accounts of the namespaces the caller owns, the built-in NS/agentiik of each among them, by namespace and then by name.

grantCreate.title: Grant creation
grantCreate.description: A grant or a deny to write at the scope the route names: one principal, and exactly one of a role and a denied permission, with an optional expiry. The scope is the route's, never the body's, so a grant cannot be written anywhere its writer does not hold grant:manage.

principal.description: Who it is for, as a principal is written: a login, group:NAME or NS/NAME. A service account of another namespace is named only where the caller sees that namespace.

role.description: The role granted, for an allow.

deny.description: The one permission taken away, for a deny, whatever any allow at any scope gives. A permission and never a role: the payloads kept out of reach are run:read_data alone, and no role is that.

expires_at.description: When it ends by itself. Absent means it lasts until revoked.

grantList.title: Grant list
grantList.description: Grants and denies, each with the scope it was written at.

grants.description: The grants and denies that apply, each with its scope, so that a list for a workflow tells what it inherits from its namespace from what is written on it. An expired grant is left out.

newPassword.title: New password
newPassword.description: A password to set, as its holder chose it: at least 12 characters, counted as Unicode code points, and at most 1,024 bytes, which the API counts on the bytes sent and refuses before anything is hashed, so that a body cannot be made to cost hashing; the maxLength here is the most characters 1,024 bytes can hold. It is not the account's login, whatever the case of its letters, which the API refuses with 422. No rule says what it is made of and none expires it, as NIST SP 800-63B tells a verifier: a digit, a capital or a symbol required makes a password harder to remember and hardly harder to guess. Hashed with Argon2id as the bytes sent, and never stored or logged as sent.

passwordEnrolRequest.title: Password enrolment request
passwordEnrolRequest.description: The code of an enrolment link or a recovery code, and the password it sets.

code.description: The code, as the enrolment page reads it after the link's # or as a recovery code is typed in. Spent by the password it sets, in the transaction that records it, and left unspent by a refusal.

passwordEnrolled.title: Password enrolled
passwordEnrolled.description: What a password set from an enrolment code did: whose it is, the password as the credentials list will show it, and what the session it opened may do, the session itself being the cookie set beside this answer.

login.description: The account the code was issued for.

session.description: full, or enrolment where the policy that applies to the account requires a passkey. Absent where the password opened no session: its user is suspended for another reason than holding no passkey, which the password does not lift.

credential.description: The password set, by the identifier removing it names; never its hash.

passwordSetRequest.title: Password request
passwordSetRequest.description: The password to set, and the current one where the account holds one.

current_password.description: The password held now, required where the account holds one and refused where it holds none. It proves possession for a change as a sign-in in the last 10 minutes proves it for a first password, and counts as a guess at it as a sign-in does. At most 1,024 bytes, as any password is.

totpStarted.title: TOTP generator started
totpStarted.description: A TOTP generator started and waiting for its first code: its secret, answered this once, and when it stops waiting.

id.description: The identifier the generator is enrolled under once confirmed, as the credentials list will show it.

secret.description: The generator's secret, 160 bits, in base32 without padding, as an authenticator application takes it typed in. Shown in this answer and never again: it is kept sealed under the master key.

uri.description: The same secret as the otpauth:// URI an authenticator application scans, which the sign-in page draws as a QR code: issued by Agentiik for LOGIN@HOST, HOST being the public URL's host, so that two installations' generators are told apart in one application, or for LOGIN alone where the host is an IPv6 address, whose colons the format cannot hold; with SHA1, 6 digits and 30 seconds, the values every application assumes, written all the same.

expires_at.description: When the generator stops waiting for its first code, ten minutes after it was started.

totpCode.title: TOTP code
totpCode.description: One code of a TOTP generator, as it shows it now.

totp.description: Six digits, the code the generator shows now; one of its step or before it, accepted already, is refused.

workflowCreate.title: Workflow creation
workflowCreate.description: A new, empty workflow repository: its name, and optionally its default branch and whether that branch is protected.

name.description: The workflow's name in the namespace, which its entry point's metadata.name will have to write.

default_branch.description: The branch HEAD names, which the first push to it creates; main where it is left out.

protected.description: Whether the default branch is protected, false where it is left out: true makes pushing to it take grant:manage, where false lets whoever holds workflow:write, an editor, push to it, as before v0.4.0. A force-push and a deletion take grant:manage either way.

workflowUpdate.title: Workflow change
workflowUpdate.description: What changes, and nothing else: a field left out keeps what is recorded.

name.description: A new name within the namespace, under workflow:write on the workflow.

namespace.description: The namespace to move the workflow to, under workflow:write on it and ownership of both namespaces, the one it leaves and the one it goes to.

default_branch.description: The branch HEAD names from now on, under grant:manage on the workflow: a branch the repository holds, or, while it holds no commit at all, the branch its first push will create.

protected.description: Whether the default branch is protected, under grant:manage on the workflow, since protection decides who may push to the branch production runs.

historyEntry.title: History entry
historyEntry.description: One commit of the default branch's first-parent history, and the version it is where it is one.

parent.description: Its first parent, which the history follows; absent for a root commit.

name.description: The git author's name, as the commit records it.

email.description: The git author's address, as the commit records it, never checked against anything.

author.description: The commit's git author, whoever the git configuration of whoever wrote it named, as distinct from the version's author, the principal who pushed it. Absent for a version sent as a tree, whose commit the repository does not hold.

authored_at.description: The author date the commit records, as git log shows it; absent where author is.

subject.description: The first line of the commit's message; absent where author is.
examples: Round VAT per line rather than per invoice

version.description: The version the commit is, where it is one: a commit a push left a branch or a tag pointing at, accepted by the hook. Absent for a commit a push only carried on the way, which no run can name.

examples.subject: Round VAT per line rather than per invoice
Split the rounding out of the charge step

workflowDetail.title: Workflow
workflowDetail.description: A workflow: its repository, the version a run naming no ref runs with the graph it resolves to, and a page of the default branch's history.

version.description: The version a run naming no ref runs: the default branch's head, or, while that branch is unborn, the latest version agk push sent as a tree before the repository's first git push. Absent where there is neither.

graph.description: The graph that version resolves to, as its push recorded it, or, for a version agk push sent as a tree, as the engine rebuilds it from what that push stored. Absent where version is, and for a library, whose root agentiik.yaml is a fragment and resolves to no graph.

history.description: A page of the default branch's first-parent history, newest first, from its head or from the commit from names; each commit a version carries it. While the default branch is unborn, the versions agk push sent as trees instead, newest first. Empty for a repository holding nothing.

examples.subject: Round VAT per line rather than per invoice
Split the rounding out of the charge step

next.description: The commit the following page starts from, for from; absent on the last page.

history.subject: Round VAT per line rather than per invoice
Split the rounding out of the charge step

treeEntry.title: Tree entry
treeEntry.description: One file of a tree, as a version's manifest records it.

path.description: Its path from the root of the tree, which is also where a step finds it under /agk/repo/.

mode.description: Its mode, one of the two git gives a file.

sha256.description: The SHA-256 of its bytes, which the object holding it is stored under and a runner fetches it by.

refs.title: Refs
refs.description: A workflow repository's branches and tags, as GET /api/v1/{ns}/workflows/{name}/refs answers them.
Every branch and tag, in git's order, byte by byte. Never empty, since the default branch is held from the repository's creation, without a commit until something is pushed to it.

tree.title: Tree
tree.description: The files of the commit a ref names.

commit.description: The commit the ref resolved to, which the listing is of.

entries.description: Every file of the tree, by path, whole: a tree holds 65,536 files at the most.

imageTag.title: Image tag
imageTag.description: An image as a step names it by a tag, or by no tag, which names latest: written as the step writes it, and never by a digest, which names one image and needs no pin. Printable ASCII, 0x21 to 0x7e, holding no @, since the OCI distribution specification's grammar is ASCII and an @ begins a digest. It names a repository, what is left once the tag, after the last colon that follows the last slash, is taken off: :1 names none and is refused, since a tag is pinned to a digest of its own repository and the digest is pulled from there. The pattern's first alternative is a reference that does not begin with a colon, and its second one that does and holds another colon or a slash after it, which leaves a repository before any tag. At most 384 bytes, which maxLength counts alike since every character is a byte: the 255 characters clients hold a registry's host and a repository's name to together, a colon, and a tag of at most 128 characters, both from the same specification.

imageDigest.title: Image by digest
imageDigest.description: An image by digest, name@sha256: and sixty-four lowercase hexadecimal characters, as the wire's imageRef writes it, and in printable ASCII, 0x21 to 0x7e, as any reference: what a tag is pinned to, and what a brick manifest is recorded under, since a digest names one image and the manifest is inside it. A tag written beside the digest is dropped: name:tag@sha256:D is kept, answered and looked up as name@sha256:D, since the digest alone names the image and a tag beside it says nothing more: one image is kept once, whichever spelling a recording or a step writes, and a step writing either finds its manifest. Held to the 384 bytes of any reference, which maxLength counts alike, and naming a repository before its digest and any tag, as imageTag does: :x@sha256:D names none and is refused, since the digest is pulled from the repository it names.

imagePin.title: Image pin
imagePin.description: One image tag of the repository and the reference by digest it is pinned to: the image a push naming the tag is judged with, and which the version it makes runs.

reference.description: The image as the workflow's steps name it, by a tag.

image.description: The reference by digest the tag is pinned to, of the tag's own repository: the reference less its tag, an @ and the digest, kept so where the recording wrote a tag beside the digest. A digest of another repository is refused, since the digest is what is pulled from where the step says the image is.

pinned_by.description: Who pinned the tag to this digest: whoever created the pin, or last moved it. Naming the pin again at the digest it holds changes neither this nor pinned_at.

pinned_at.description: When the tag was pinned to this digest.

brickManifest.title: Recorded brick manifest
brickManifest.description: The brick manifest the repository holds for one image, by digest, told by the SHA-256 of its text rather than the text: what a brick step running that image is held to at a push, and what the version that push makes keeps of the brick, from which a run takes where each secret is mounted and how each parameter is checked. The text is the file the image holds at /agk/brick.yaml, which is where to read it.

image.description: The image, by digest, whose /agk/brick.yaml the manifest is: less any tag the recording wrote beside the digest, as it is kept and looked up.

sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the manifest as kept, the text of /agk/brick.yaml byte for byte, in lowercase hexadecimal, computed by the database so that a listing never reads the text: a reader tells from it whether what is kept is the image's own file, and which image.manifest entry of the audit log recorded it, and agk push leaves out of a recording a manifest the repository already holds, rather than send it again at every push.

recorded_by.description: Who recorded the manifest held: whoever recorded it first, or last replaced it with other bytes. Recording the same bytes again changes neither this nor recorded_at. The audit log names every one who recorded it, as image.manifest, where this names the last.

recorded_at.description: When the manifest held was recorded.

imagesRecord.title: Image pins and brick manifests to record
imagesRecord.description: What a recording adds to the repository: pins, manifests or both, naming at least one entry between them, since a recording of nothing is a client's mistake rather than a request. Whatever the body leaves out stays as the repository holds it.

pins.description: Each image a step names by a tag, mapped to the reference by digest to pin it to, of the tag's own repository: the digest the pusher's Docker daemon resolved the tag to. A value written name:tag@sha256:D is pinned as name@sha256:D. A tag already pinned moves to the digest named. At most 256, one for each image a workflow names.

additionalProperties.description: A brick manifest, the text of the /agk/brick.yaml the image holds, kept byte for byte: at most 256 KiB, and never empty. maxLength counts characters, and the API counts the bytes.
