images.title: Image pins and brick manifests
images.description: A repository's image pins and brick manifests, each manifest without its text: every one it holds, as the GET answers them, or only those a recording named, read back as they now stand, as the POST answers them.

pins.description: The pins, by reference in byte order. Empty where the repository holds none, or the recording named none.

manifests.description: The manifests, by image in byte order. Empty where the repository holds none, or the recording named none.

statsPercentiles.title: Percentiles
statsPercentiles.description: Three percentiles of a length of time, in whole milliseconds, taken over what the bucket counts. Each is absent where the bucket counts nothing to take it over, which a chart draws as a gap rather than as zero.

statsExitCodes.title: Attempts by exit code
statsExitCodes.description: Attempts counted by the exit code they ended with, the most frequent first, one entry a code. An attempt that ended with none, lost with its runner or stopped at its deadline, is counted under null.

items.description: The attempts that ended with one exit code.

exit_code.description: The exit code, or null for an attempt that ended with none.

attempts.description: How many attempts ended with it.

statsRunsBucket.title: A bucket of runs
statsRunsBucket.description: What the runs created in one bucket came to.

since.description: Where the bucket starts, included: the since GET /api/v1/runs takes.

until.description: The last instant of the bucket, included, a nanosecond before the next one starts: the until GET /api/v1/runs takes, so that a point opens exactly the runs it counts.

runs.description: The runs created in the bucket, by state: a run that has ended under its final state, one still going under where it is now, so that the counts add up to what GET /api/v1/runs lists over the bucket. The share that did not succeed is failed, cancelled and timed_out over the runs that ended, which a client works out.

duration_ms.description: How long the runs of the bucket that ended took, from started_at to finished_at, so that the time a run queued behind a quota is not counted as its own. Absent where none has ended.

queue_wait_ms.description: How long the tasks of those runs waited, from when each could be handed out to its dispatch: the time a runner took to have room. A task can be handed out from its creation or, for a further attempt, from the end of its retry's backoff, which is the step's policy rather than a wait for room. A task written before v0.6.0 recorded neither and counts no wait. Absent where no task was dispatched.

retries.description: The attempts that were retried, by the exit code of the attempt that failed. Empty where nothing was retried.

statsRuns.title: Run statistics
statsRuns.description: The runs of a namespace's workflows, bucket by bucket, over the range: only the workflows the caller holds run:read on, as GET /api/v1/runs lists them, so that a chart shows nothing a list would not.

from.description: The start of the range, included, as the request gave it or as it was taken.

to.description: The end of the range, excluded.

bucket.description: How long a bucket is, as asked or as the range chose.

workflow.description: The workflow the series are narrowed to, where the request named one.

buckets.description: Every bucket of the range, oldest first, those counting nothing included, so that a chart's points are evenly spaced.

overall.description: The range as one bucket, from the first bucket's since to the last one's until: what its runs came to together, which a figure beside the charts reads. Its counts are the buckets' summed, and its percentiles are taken over the whole range rather than combined from the buckets', which percentiles do not combine into, so a client could not work them out.

items.description: One bin: the runs whose duration falls in it.

from_ms.description: The shortest duration of the bin, included, in milliseconds.

until_ms.description: The longest, excluded, save for the last bin, which holds the longest run.

runs.description: How many runs took that long.

histogram.description: The durations of the runs that ended over the range, in the bins histogram asked for, shortest first; fewer where the runs are fewer than the bins, and empty where none has ended. Present where histogram was asked for.

from.description: The start of the span before, included: from minus as many buckets as the range takes, which is from minus the range's length where from and to fall on bucket boundaries.

to.description: The end of the span before, excluded: to minus as many buckets as the range takes, which is the range's from where from and to fall on bucket boundaries.

buckets.description: The buckets of the span before, as many as the range's, ending where the range's first begins.

overall.description: The span before as one bucket, as overall is the range's: what a figure's change is worked out against.

items.description: One bin: the runs whose duration falls in it.

from_ms.description: The shortest duration of the bin, included, in milliseconds.

until_ms.description: The longest, excluded, save for the last bin, which holds the longest run.

runs.description: How many runs took that long.

histogram.description: The durations of the runs that ended over the range, in the bins histogram asked for, shortest first; fewer where the runs are fewer than the bins, and empty where none has ended. Present where histogram was asked for.

previous.description: The span just before the range, in as many buckets of the same length, with its histogram where one was asked for. Present where compare=previous.

statsStepBucket.title: A bucket of one step
statsStepBucket.description: What one step came to in the runs created in one bucket.

since.description: Where the bucket starts, included: the since GET /api/v1/runs takes.

until.description: The last instant of the bucket, included, a nanosecond before the next one starts: the until GET /api/v1/runs takes, so that a point opens exactly the runs it counts.

duration_ms.description: How long its attempts that ended ran, from their last dispatch to their end, each shard of a fan-out an attempt of its own: a lost dispatch handed out again is the same attempt. Absent where none ended.

attempts.description: How many attempts it was handed out, retries and shards included, one still running among them.

exit_codes.description: The attempts that ended, by the exit code of their last dispatch, 0 among them: one still running is counted in attempts and not here.

items_per_minute.description: For a step that fans out, the items its shards consumed a minute while any of them ran, over the runs created in the bucket: the items of the shards that succeeded, each the longest of its input ports, which is what a fan-out cuts on, over the time any dispatch of a shard ran, a minute two ran side by side counted once. Absent for any other step, and where no shard ran.

statsStepHour.title: One hour of the week of one step
statsStepHour.description: One cell of the heatmap: the attempts of the step in the runs created over the range that ended, by the weekday and the hour of the day of their last dispatch, in UTC.

weekday.description: The day of the week, 1 for Monday to 7 for Sunday, as ISO 8601 numbers them.

hour.description: The hour of the day, in UTC.

duration_ms.description: The median of how long those attempts ran. Absent where the cell counts none.

statsSteps.title: Step statistics
statsSteps.description: The steps of one workflow over the range, bucket by bucket or, with by=hour, by weekday and hour.

from.description: The start of the range, included, as the request gave it or as it was taken.

to.description: The end of the range, excluded.

bucket.description: How long a bucket is. Absent with by=hour.

by.description: hour, where the request asked for the heatmap.

items.description: One step of the workflow, as its latest version names it.

buckets.description: Every bucket of the range, oldest first. Absent with by=hour.

overall.description: The range as one bucket, from the first bucket's since to the last one's until: what the step came to over the whole range, which a figure beside the charts reads. Its attempts and exit codes are the buckets' summed, and its percentiles and its items a minute are taken over the whole range, since neither combines from the buckets'. Absent with by=hour.

hours.description: The 168 cells, Monday at midnight first. Present with by=hour alone.

previous.description: The buckets of the span just before the range. Present where compare=previous.

previous_overall.description: The span before as one bucket, as overall is the range's: what a figure's change is worked out against. Present where compare=previous.

steps.description: The steps of the workflow in the order its latest version runs them, upstream first and those no edge orders by name, then, by name, a step it no longer declares where the range reaches runs of an older version. The latest version is the head of the default branch, or, for a workflow no git push has filled, the last version a tree push recorded. A graph keeps no order of declaration, so the order is the one a reader of the workflow meets its steps in.

statsPortBucket.title: A bucket of one step's ports
statsPortBucket.description: What one step published in the runs created in one bucket.

since.description: Where the bucket starts, included: the since GET /api/v1/runs takes.

until.description: The last instant of the bucket, included, a nanosecond before the next one starts: the until GET /api/v1/runs takes, so that a point opens exactly the runs it counts.

items.description: The items published on each output port of the step, summed over the runs created in the bucket, from the count each envelope's meta.count gives and the step's record keeps, and never from its items, so that run:read_data is never asked. Every port the latest version declares on the step is named, 0 where it published nothing, and so is a port an older version declared that a run in the range published on. The share rejected, or sent to error, is what the rejected or the error port published over what every output port of the step did, which a client works out.

statsPorts.title: Port statistics
statsPorts.description: What each step of one workflow published, port by port, bucket by bucket, over the range.

from.description: The start of the range, included, as the request gave it or as it was taken.

to.description: The end of the range, excluded.

bucket.description: How long a bucket is, as asked or as the range chose.

buckets.description: Every bucket of the range, oldest first.

previous.description: The buckets of the span just before the range. Present where compare=previous.

steps.description: The steps of the workflow in the order its latest version runs them, upstream first and those no edge orders by name, then, by name, a step it no longer declares where the range reaches runs of an older version, as GET /api/v1/{ns}/stats/steps orders them.

statsQuotaBucket.title: A bucket of a namespace's load
statsQuotaBucket.description: What the namespace asked of its quotas in one bucket.

since.description: Where the bucket starts, included: the since GET /api/v1/runs takes.

until.description: The last instant of the bucket, included, a nanosecond before the next one starts: the until GET /api/v1/runs takes, so that a point opens exactly the runs it counts.

runs_created.description: The runs created in the bucket, whoever created them, against max_runs_per_hour.

runs_refused.description: The runs refused for max_runs_per_hour in the bucket, whatever asked for them: a request answered 429, a schedule or an event firing recorded as skipped, or a call failed. A refusal is counted where it is decided, a minute at a time.

tasks_in_flight_max.description: The most tasks handed out, or on their way to a runner, and not yet ended at once in the bucket, which is what max_concurrent_tasks counts: one ending as another is handed out is not two at once, and one still running is in flight until now.

artifact_bytes.description: The bytes max_artifact_bytes counted at the bucket's end: the namespace's artifacts written by then and neither expired nor retired, each digest once.

artifact_bytes_added.description: The bytes of the artifacts written in the bucket, each digest once.

statsQuotas.title: Quota statistics
statsQuotas.description: A namespace's load, bucket by bucket, beside the quotas it meets. Whoever reads the namespace reads it, since a quota bounds every workflow of it alike.

from.description: The start of the range, included, as the request gave it or as it was taken.

to.description: The end of the range, excluded.

bucket.description: How long a bucket is, as asked or as the range chose.

quotas.description: The namespace's quotas as they stand now, which a chart draws as the line each series runs under: an earlier value is the audit log's to tell. A quota that bounds nothing is absent, as GET /api/v1/namespaces/{ns}/quotas answers it.

buckets.description: Every bucket of the range, oldest first.

from.description: The start of the span before, included: from minus as many buckets as the range takes, which is from minus the range's length where from and to fall on bucket boundaries.

to.description: The end of the span before, excluded: to minus as many buckets as the range takes, which is the range's from where from and to fall on bucket boundaries.

buckets.description: The buckets of the span before, as many as the range's, ending where the range's first begins.

previous.description: The span just before the range, in as many buckets of the same length. Present where compare=previous.

statsActivityBucket.title: A bucket of the installation's activity
statsActivityBucket.description: What every namespace together did in one bucket, in counts alone.

since.description: Where the bucket starts, included: the since GET /api/v1/runs takes.

until.description: The last instant of the bucket, included, a nanosecond before the next one starts: the until GET /api/v1/runs takes.

runs.description: The runs created in the bucket in every namespace, by state: a run that has ended under its final state, one still going under where it is now. A namespace's runs count within its retention, as in every series.

tasks_in_flight_max.description: The most tasks handed out, or on their way to a runner, and not yet ended at once in the bucket, in every namespace together: one ending as another is handed out is not two at once, and one still running is in flight until now.

statsActivityNow.title: What the installation is doing now
statsActivityNow.description: What every namespace together is doing as the request is answered.

runs.description: The runs not ended, in every namespace, by state, whenever they were created.

tasks_in_flight.description: The tasks handed out, or on their way to a runner, and not yet ended.

slots.description: The tasks the runners counted in runners_ready offer to run at once together: what tasks_in_flight is set against.

runners_ready.description: The runners that may be handed work: ready, reporting themselves ready, and heard from within 30 s, after which a runner's tasks are declared lost.

runners.description: The runners not revoked, ready or not.

statsActivity.title: The installation's activity
statsActivity.description: What every namespace together did, bucket by bucket, and what it is doing now, in counts that name no run, workflow or namespace. Administrator only. compare=previous is not taken.

from.description: The start of the range, included, as the request gave it or as it was taken.

to.description: The end of the range, excluded.

bucket.description: How long a bucket is, as asked or as the range chose.

buckets.description: Every bucket of the range, oldest first, those counting nothing included.

now.description: What the installation is doing as the request is answered.

statsSlotBucket.title: A bucket of slots
statsSlotBucket.description: A pool's or a runner's slots in one bucket.

since.description: Where the bucket starts, included: the since GET /api/v1/runs takes.

until.description: The last instant of the bucket, included, a nanosecond before the next one starts: the until GET /api/v1/runs takes, so that a point opens exactly the runs it counts.

slots_in_use_max.description: The most slots in use at once in the bucket: the tasks held from when the runner redeemed each to when it ended, one ending as another is taken not two at once.

capacity.description: The slots offered at the bucket's end, which falls as a runner drains and to 0 once it has left.

statsPools.title: Pool statistics
statsPools.description: Every pool's slots and each of its runners', bucket by bucket, and every silence between a runner's heartbeats over the range. Administrator only. compare=previous is not taken: what a chart of the pools sets a runner against is its capacity.

from.description: The start of the range, included, as the request gave it or as it was taken.

to.description: The end of the range, excluded.

bucket.description: How long a bucket is, as asked or as the range chose.

buckets.description: The pool's slots, every bucket of the range, oldest first: the most its runners held at once together, and what they offered together at the bucket's end.

items.description: One runner of the pool, one that was in it at any time over the range included.

runner.description: The runner, by the name it joined under.

buckets.description: Its slots, every bucket of the range, oldest first: a task holds one from when the runner redeemed it to when it ended, or until now, and the runner offers its concurrency while it is ready and reports itself ready, nothing while it is drained, draining, unhealthy or revoked, and nothing once silent for 30 s.

items.description: One silence between two heartbeats of 20 s or more, two intervals: those of 30 s and more are the ones after which the runner's tasks are declared lost.

at.description: When the silence began: the last heartbeat before it.

length_ms.description: How long it lasted, in milliseconds, until the next heartbeat or the end of the range for one still going.

tasks_lost.description: The tasks declared lost because of it, and handed out again.

silences.description: Every silence that began over the range, oldest first.

runList.title: Run list
runList.description: Runs as the caller may read them, newest first by when they were created.

runs.description: The runs of the workflows the caller holds run:read on, narrowed as the query asks, newest first. Empty where nothing matches, a namespace or a workflow the caller cannot read included.

envelopeReference.title: Envelope reference
envelopeReference.description: An envelope as the database keeps it: its digest, its size and how many items it holds, never its items. The bytes are in the object store, read with run:read_data by the routes that answer an envelope; this is what run:read sees of one.

digest.description: The envelope's digest, which names it in the object store and is kept after its bytes are purged.

items.description: How many items the envelope holds, from its meta.count.

purged_at.description: When the bytes behind the digest were purged with the run's retention. Absent while they are there.

stepSummary.title: Step summary
stepSummary.description: One step of a run as a screen shows it: its verdict, how many attempts it took, when it ran, and the envelope each of its output ports published.

step.description: The step, by the name the workflow file gives it.

verdict.description: Where the step stands: pending before it starts, or while it waits for another attempt; running while a shard of it is in flight; succeeded once it published its ports; failed, which continue_on_error does not change; skipped where its if was false; cancelled with its run, where it was under way when the run was cancelled or timed out, a step nobody reached staying pending.

attempts.description: How many attempts the step has been given, 0 before its first.

started_at.description: When its first attempt started. Absent before.

finished_at.description: When it reached its verdict. Absent while it has none.

ports.description: The envelope each output port published, by port. Absent before the step published anything.

image.description: The image the step runs, by digest, as the version the run pinned resolved it: an image the file named by a tag is the digest the tag was resolved to when the version was pushed. Absent for a workflow step, which runs no container, and where the version can no longer be read.

input_ports.description: The input ports the step declares, by name, sorted: those its edges feed and those its inputs keyword feeds, each handed to a task as an envelope, empty ones included. Absent for a step that reads nothing.

output_ports.description: The output ports the step declares, in the order the file writes them: each is published once, when the step ends, an empty envelope where nothing was written to it, which is what ports carries from then on.

taskSummary.title: Task summary
taskSummary.description: One task of a run, which is one shard of one attempt of one step: where it stands, which runner held it, how it ended, and the envelopes it was handed.

task.description: The task's identifier: the run, the step and the attempt, run/step/attempt, and the shard's index and cardinality after them, run/step/attempt/index/of, where a fan-out produced it.

step.description: The step it is an attempt of.

attempt.description: Which attempt of its step it is, counted from one, as AGK_ATTEMPT carries it.

shard.description: Which shard of a fan-out it is. Absent where the step is not fanned out.

runner.description: The runner that held it, by name, never its host. Absent before one held it, and for a cache hit or a call, which no runner holds.

exit_code.description: The exit code its ending carries, a stopped container's included, where a container started and reported one, or where the engine could not build the task, which is 120. Absent otherwise.

started_at.description: When its container started. Absent before.

finished_at.description: When it ended. Absent while it has not.

memoised_from.description: For a cache hit, which republished envelopes without starting a container, the run whose task published them.

called.description: For a workflow: step's task, the run the call started, whose ending is this task's.

inputs.description: The envelopes the task was handed on its input ports, by digest, from the grant it was dispatched with. Absent for a task never dispatched.

params.description: The parameters the task was dispatched with, resolved: every expression evaluated and the matrix combination in, as the container read them from /agk/params.json, a secret written as {"secret": name} and never as its value. An expression may carry envelope contents into them, so they are answered only to a caller holding run:read_data on the run's workflow, and otherwise left out; absent for a task never dispatched, a cache hit and a call.

runDetail.title: Run detail
runDetail.description: One run whole: the record the listing gives, then what became of every part of it, its steps and each of their tasks, the envelopes they published and were handed by digest, and why it ended where nothing in its workflow ended it. Its inputs are envelope contents, answered only to a caller holding run:read_data on the run's workflow.

namespace.description: The namespace the run is in.

workflow.description: The workflow it is a run of.

commit.description: The commit the run is pinned to.

triggered_by.description: The principal the run is attributed to.

from.description: The run and the step that called this one, for a run whose trigger_kind is workflow.

started_at.description: When it was let in. Absent while it is queued.

finished_at.description: When it ended. Absent while it has not.

inputs.description: What the run was started with, each workflow input as it was given. Envelope contents, so answered only to a caller holding run:read_data on the run's workflow, and otherwise left out, as for a run started with none.

additionalProperties.description: A declared output: the step and the port it is a view of, and how many items that port published.

step.description: The step the output is a view of.

outputs.description: The run's declared outputs, recorded when it succeeds with every one of them published, by name. Absent before.

replay_from_start_only.description: Whether an input a step could restart from has been purged, so that the run replays from its start only and a screen does not offer a step.

replay_of.description: For a replay, the run it replays.

replay_from.description: For a replay from a step, that step: the steps above it were reused rather than run, and carry a verdict and no task. Absent for a replay from the start.

items.description: One workflow include of the version the run pinned.

workflow.description: The workflow the file included, NS/NAME as it wrote it.

commit.description: The commit the ref resolved to when the version was pushed.

includes.description: The workflow includes of the version the run pinned, each with the commit its ref resolved to. Absent where it includes no other repository.

reason.description: Why the run ended as it did, where nothing in its workflow is what ended it: a run its principal no longer held workflow:run for when it was created. Absent on every other run.
examples: alice no longer holds workflow:run on finance/monthly-invoicing: the grant that gave it expired at 2026-10-01T05:00:00Z

steps.description: Every step of the run, each with its verdict.

tasks.description: Every task of the run, each shard of each attempt of each step.

artifacts.description: The files the run's steps published, live or retired, by step, port and name: what each envelope's files name, with where each stands in its retention. Empty for a run that published none.

runAsked.title: Run asked
runAsked.description: That a cancellation was asked of a run, and which: never how the run stands, which run:read guards and this route does not.

replayRequest.title: Replay request
replayRequest.description: Where a replay starts: a step, reusing every step above it, or the start where no step is named.

step.description: The step the replay runs from. The steps it reads from, directly or through others, are reused, their verdicts and envelopes taken from the run replayed. Left out, the replay runs from the start and reuses nothing.

replayStarted.title: Replay started
replayStarted.description: The run a replay started, a new run of the commit the one replayed pinned, over the inputs it was started with, attributed to whoever asked.

state.description: Where it stands as it is written.

commit.description: The commit it runs, the one the run replayed pinned.

replay_from.description: The step it replays from. Absent for a replay from the start.

runArtifact.title: Run artifact
runArtifact.description: One file a step of the run published on a port, as its reference holds it: what the envelope's file names, and where it stands in its retention. The reference outlives the bytes, so that a file fetched past its retention answers 410 rather than 404 and the run keeps showing its name, size and digest with its collection recorded.

uri.description: The URI the envelope names it by, which GET /api/v1/artifacts/{uri} fetches it with.

port.description: The port it was published on.

name.description: Its name on that port, the last segment of its URI.

size.description: How many bytes it holds, kept once the bytes are gone.

sha256.description: The SHA-256 digest of its bytes, kept once the bytes are gone.

status.description: live while it may be fetched; expired once its duration ran out; collected once the fetches its budget allowed were spent. A retired reference is kept rather than deleted, which is what the run detail reads.

expires_at.description: When it stops being fetchable, its retain capped by the namespace's max_retention_days when it was written: an output's own retain where it declares one, defaults.retain otherwise. Absent where nothing bounds it, neither a retain nor the namespace: the file is kept for ever.

retired_at.description: When it stopped being live. Absent while it is.

fetches_left.description: What remains of a fetch budget, which only a workflow output declaring retain with fetches carries. Absent where there is none.

startRequest.title: Start request
startRequest.description: What a run is asked for: the commit it runs, named or reached through a ref, or neither for the default branch's head, and the workflow inputs it is started with, bound against that version's declaration as agk run --local binds them. {} asks for the head with no input. A commit and a ref together are refused, since a run is of one commit.

commit.description: A commit that is a version of the workflow.

ref.description: A branch or a tag by its short name or in full, or a whole commit that is a version, resolved once, when the run is asked for: the run is pinned to the commit it names then, whatever the ref does next.

inputs.description: The workflow inputs by name, each held to its JSON Schema, a default filling one left out, and recorded as bound. At most as many values as one envelope may carry items, and as many bytes as one envelope may weigh: a run's data belongs in an artifact. null is read as none.

runStarted.title: Run started
runStarted.description: The run a request started, attributed to the caller as a manual run, written and not yet begun: what happens to it is the controller's.

state.description: Where it stands as it is written.

commit.description: The commit it is pinned to, which a caller naming a ref, or none, did not name.

inputRefusal.title: Input refused
inputRefusal.description: An input the request gets wrong: the sentence agk run --local prints for it, and the input and the rule apart, so that a form can point at its field without reading the sentence.

examples: input orders: schema: /0/amount: got string, want number; run refused

input.description: The input, by the name the request or the declaration gives it.

rule.description: The key a person finds in the workflow file: required for an input left out with no default, schema for a value its JSON Schema refuses, undeclared for a name the workflow does not declare.

examples.error: input orders: schema: /0/amount: got string, want number; run refused
input orders: required: no value supplied and the input declares no default; run refused

secretDeclaration.title: Secret declaration
secretDeclaration.description: One secret as the routes answer it: its name, the store its value is kept in and where in it, and where a step is given it. Never its value, which no route reads.

name.description: The secret's name, as the workflow file names it.

provider.description: The store its value is kept in: builtin, the encrypted store, which keeps it sealed under the namespace and the name; env, the API's own environment, for development, where the installation has opted the namespace in; or vault, which no installation reads from until its provider arrives.

path.description: Where the value sits inside its store: an environment variable's name for env, beginning with the prefix the installation gives the namespace. Absent for builtin, which keeps a value under the namespace and the name and takes no path.

mount.description: Where a step is given the value, as a file on tmpfs, where its brick's manifest names no mount of its own: /agk/secrets/<name>. Answered rather than stored, since it follows from the name, and answered at all because the file a brick reads is what a person looking at a declaration is usually trying to find.

secretList.title: Secret list
secretList.description: A namespace's secret declarations, by name.

secrets.description: Every declaration of the namespace, never a value.

secretDeclare.title: Secret declaration written
secretDeclare.description: What a PUT writes: the store a value is kept in, where in it, and for builtin the value itself, written once and returned by no answer. A PUT naming builtin without a value keeps the value stored; rotating is sending one again, never reading one first. A secret moved out of builtin, or removed, takes its stored value with it.

provider.description: The store: builtin, env where the installation has opted the namespace in, or vault, refused until its provider arrives, since nothing gives a namespace its prefix in Vault before then.

path.description: For env, the variable the value is read from, which begins with the prefix the installation gives the namespace. Refused for builtin, which takes none.

value.description: The value, for builtin alone, at most 1 MiB once decoded. No answer carries it, now or later, and an empty one is refused rather than taken for a PUT that keeps the old one.

encoding.description: How value is written: utf-8 where absent, or base64 for a value that is not text, a keystore for instance, since JSON carries no arbitrary bytes.

variableList.title: Variable list
variableList.description: A namespace's variables, by name, whole and not paged: a namespace holds at most 1,000.

variables.description: Every variable of the namespace, sorted by name, each with its value.

variableWrite.title: Variable written
variableWrite.description: What a PUT writes: the whole variable, its value, its visibility and for selected its workflows, each written every time, so that a PUT changing only the value never leaves the visibility to a default that could widen a variable selected for one workflow to every workflow of the namespace.

value.description: Any JSON value, null among them, at most 64 KiB written as compact JSON. A number is held as a run's inputs are: one no 64-bit float holds, or written past 340 digits from the point, is refused, and one written with an exponent is written out with a point, 1e3 as 1000.0, so that it reads back a double. U+0000 in a string or a name is refused, since PostgreSQL does not keep it in JSON.

visibility.description: all, read by every workflow of the namespace, or selected, read by those workflows names.

items.description: A workflow of the namespace by name, one not pushed yet included.

workflows.description: For selected alone, and required with it, the workflows that read it, each once, in any order, kept sorted; [] for none. Required rather than taken as none where left out, so that a PUT forgetting it does not empty the list, and refused beside all.

runner.title: Runner
runner.description: One runner as the inventory holds it: its identifier, pool and labels, what the host has, what the installation and the runner each say of its state, and who took it out of service and when. Never the host it runs on, nor the key it joined with, which proves it rather than lists it: a runner is a name, a pool and labels, so that a host can be reimaged or moved while what is written against the fleet stays true.
The identifier the API minted at the join, a lowercase ULID: the name a run gives the runner of each task, and the only one.

pool.description: The pool it joined, the one its join token was issued from.

labels.description: The labels it joined with, each one its pool carries and its join token permitted: what a step's runs_on selects it by. Empty for a runner that claimed none.

cpu.description: The host's virtual cores, as the agent measured them at the join.

memory_bytes.description: The host's memory in bytes, as the agent measured it at the join.

disk_bytes.description: The disk its working directory may use, in bytes, as the agent measured it at the join.

architecture.description: What the host runs, as the agent reported it at the join.

agent_version.description: The agent's version, as it last reported it: at the join, then at each heartbeat, since an agent upgraded in place is the same runner.

namespaces.description: The namespaces the host's own policy accepts, where it narrows its pool's; absent where it narrows nothing, which is the ordinary case.

containment.description: What the host reported at the join about how a container is contained on it; absent where it reported nothing.

state.description: The installation's word on the runner, which is the one obeyed: ready, draining once an administrator drained it, revoked once one revoked it. What the runner says of itself is reported_state.

reported_state.description: What the runner said of itself at its last heartbeat: ready, draining, or unhealthy where it took itself out of service. Recorded and never obeyed. Absent until its first heartbeat.

concurrency.description: The most tasks it runs at once, as it reported it at its last heartbeat. Absent until its first heartbeat.

drain_reason.description: Why it was taken out of service, in the order's words, one line: a drain's, or a revocation's, which replaces it.

drained_by.description: Who ordered the drain, present with drained_at once one was ordered. An order given twice keeps the first.

revoked_by.description: Who revoked it, present with revoked_at once it is revoked.

results_accepted_until.description: The end of a revocation's grace, fixed at the revocation: the results of the tasks it still holds are taken until then, and it is refused everywhere after. Present only for a revoked runner.

last_seen_at.description: Its last heartbeat, by the installation's clock. Absent until its first; three intervals with none move its tasks to lost.

rotate_by.description: When its credential has to have been rotated by; past it, the credential is refused.

runnerList.title: Runner inventory
runnerList.description: Every runner of the installation, revoked ones included, by pool and then by identifier.

runners.description: The runners, in the order of their pool's name and then their identifier.

runnerPoolList.title: Runner pool list
runnerPoolList.description: Every runner pool of the installation, by name.

runner_pools.description: The pools, each as the wire writes one with its token half absent, since a listing issues no join token. Every field is written, containment included, so that nobody reading a pool has to know a default.

profileUpdate.title: Profile change
profileUpdate.description: What changes of the caller's profile, and nothing else: a field left out keeps what is recorded, and the empty string clears a field. Null is refused rather than read as either, since a client could have meant both. The display name is not among it, being made of the given and family names, and neither is the email address, which an administrator gives.

given_name.description: The name the user is called by, the first half of their display name; the empty string clears it.

family_name.description: The user's family name, the second half of their display name; the empty string clears it.

title.description: What the user does, as they put it; the empty string clears it.

location.description: Where the user works, as they put it; the empty string clears it.

timezone.description: The time zone the user works in, a name the IANA database holds, Local refused; the empty string clears it.

bio.description: A line the user writes about themself, 280 characters at most; the empty string clears it.
examples: Writes the invoicing workflows, and reviews what touches payroll.

joinTokenRequest.title: Join token request
joinTokenRequest.description: What a join token is asked for with: the labels the machine it is meant for may claim, every one of them a label its pool carries, and how long the administrator needs to get it there. Both may be left out: a token permitting no label, which is what a runner of the pool default claims, and the default life of an hour.

labels.description: The labels a runner joining with the token may claim, a subset of its pool's: a label reaches a machine only where an administrator wrote it on a pool first, and a token narrows that further to the one machine it is meant for.

expires_in_seconds.description: How long the token lives, at most a day, an hour where it is left out: a join token only has to survive the minutes between an administrator copying it and a machine presenting it.

runnerOrder.title: Runner order
runnerOrder.description: An administrator's order to a runner, drain or revoke, and why: the reason is handed to the runner at its next heartbeat, which writes it to its own log, since whoever owns the machine is rarely whoever gave the order.

reason.description: Why, in one line of at most 256 characters: one line of a journal, which is where the runner writes it, and short enough for the console to show beside the runner.

auditPage.title: Audit page
auditPage.description: A page of the audit log, the newest entries first, with where the chain stands: the last entry appended and the last one proved, so that a reader tells an entry the chain is known to hold from one the next term checks.

entries.description: The entries of the page, the newest first; a page shorter than its limit is the last.

head.description: The last entry appended, 0 where the log is empty, whatever the page holds.

verified.description: The last entry the leading controller proved the chain to, at the start of its term: an entry after it holds as far as anybody has looked, and the next term checks it.

ns.name: ns
ns.description: The namespace, by name, or by a name it held before it was renamed, which reaches it as its name does, so that an address written before a rename keeps working. One the caller cannot see is answered as one that does not exist, so that no name can be learnt by asking.

workflow.name: name
workflow.description: The workflow, by the name its metadata.name writes. One the caller cannot see is answered as one that does not exist.

grant.name: id
grant.description: The grant's identifier, as the list gives it and as Terraform imports it.

token.name: id
token.description: The token's identifier, as the list gives it. It is not the token and opens nothing.

group.name: group
group.description: The group, by name, without the group: a principal reference writes before it.

serviceAccountNamespace.name: ns
serviceAccountNamespace.description: The namespace the service account belongs to, the half of NS/NAME before the slash. One the caller does not own is answered as one that does not exist.

serviceAccountName.name: name
serviceAccountName.description: The service account's name, the half of NS/NAME after the slash.

credential.name: id
credential.description: The credential, by the identifier GET /api/v1/me/credentials lists it with: a passkey's credential ID, or the identifier the engine minted for a password or a TOTP generator.

redirectUri.name: redirect_uri
redirectUri.description: The loopback address agk login listens on, where it opened the page. Given with code_challenge or not at all.

codeChallenge.name: code_challenge
codeChallenge.description: The SHA-256 of agk login's verifier, where it opened the page. Given with redirect_uri or not at all.

notification.name: id
notification.description: The notification's identifier, as GET /api/v1/me lists it.

asset.name: name
asset.description: The file, by its name: the page's stylesheet, page.css, and its three scripts, page.js, codec.js and qr.js, as the page links to them.

ref.name: ref
ref.description: A branch or a tag, by its short name or written in full, or a commit written whole that is a version of the workflow. A name a branch and a tag both hold is refused with 400 rather than guessed at. A ref holding a slash is written with it, the rest of the path being the ref, or with each slash percent-encoded, as a generated client writes it.

treePath.name: path
treePath.description: One file of the tree, by its path from the root, as the listing writes it: its bytes are answered rather than the listing.

historyFrom.name: from
historyFrom.description: The commit the history is listed from, itself included: the next of the page before. The default branch's head where it is left out.

historyLimit.name: limit
historyLimit.description: How many commits a page lists, 50 where it is left out and 500 at the most, as GET /api/v1/runs lists runs.

statsFrom.name: from
statsFrom.description: The start of the range, included, in RFC 3339. Where it is left out the range is the 24 hours before to, and where both are left out the last 24 hours. Refused with 400 where it is not before to, and beside range=max.

statsRange.name: range
statsRange.description: max starts the range at the first thing the route counts before to, in place of from: the first run created among those it counts, or refused for /quotas, which counts refusals too, and for /api/v1/stats/pools the first capacity a runner reported, so that the whole of what an installation kept is read at once rather than guessed at with a span. It reaches back 1,000 buckets at most, the range then starting where the 1,000th does, and where there is nothing to count it is the 24 hours before to. Refused with 400 beside from, since both say where the range starts. The answer's from is where it started. The only value.

statsTo.name: to
statsTo.description: The end of the range, excluded, in RFC 3339: now where it is left out.

statsBucket.name: bucket
statsBucket.description: How long a bucket is: 1m, 15m, 1h or 1d. Where it is left out it follows the range, so that a chart holds a few hundred points at most: a minute up to two hours, 15 minutes up to two days, an hour up to 14 days, a day beyond. Buckets fall on whole minutes, quarters, hours and days in UTC, the first holding from and the last the instant before to. Refused with 400 where the range would take more than 1,000, which no chart draws and which a query would pay for all the same.

statsCompare.name: compare
statsCompare.description: previous adds the span just before the range, in as many buckets of the same length, under previous, so that a chart draws it behind point for point and a figure shows its change. The only value.

statsWorkflowFilter.name: workflow
statsWorkflowFilter.description: Narrows the series to one workflow of the namespace. One the caller does not hold run:read on counts nothing, as a workflow that does not exist does, rather than being refused: GET /api/v1/runs lists nothing for it either.

statsWorkflow.name: workflow
statsWorkflow.description: The workflow whose steps the series are of: a step belongs to one workflow, so this route reads one. Refused with 400 where it is left out, and answered 404, as a workflow that does not exist, where the caller does not hold run:read on it.

statsHistogram.name: histogram
statsHistogram.description: Adds histogram: the durations of the runs that ended over the range in this many bins of one width, from the shortest to the longest. At most 100, which is more than a chart has room to draw; refused with 400 past it or below 1.

statsBy.name: by
statsBy.description: hour answers, instead of buckets, each step's p50 by weekday and hour of the day over the range, in UTC: 168 cells, a heatmap's, which bucket then does not shape and compare does not take. The only value.

runsNamespace.name: namespace
runsNamespace.description: Narrows the listing to one namespace. One the caller cannot read lists what one that does not exist lists, nothing, rather than being refused, so that no name can be learnt by asking.

runsWorkflow.name: workflow
runsWorkflow.description: Narrows the listing to the workflows of that name, in the namespace given or in every one the caller reads. One the caller does not hold run:read on lists nothing, as one that does not exist does.

runsState.name: state
runsState.description: Narrows the listing to the runs in one state. A word that is no run state is refused with 400.

runsSince.name: since
runsSince.description: The runs created at this instant or after it, in RFC 3339. A value that is no such time is refused with 400.

a day.summary: from the start of a day

runsUntil.name: until
runsUntil.description: The runs created at this instant or before it, in RFC 3339, both bounds being included. A statistics bucket carries the since and until that open the runs it counts.

a bucket's end.summary: the last nanosecond of a day

runsLimit.name: limit
runsLimit.description: How many runs at most, newest first: 50 when left out, and at most 500. A limit outside 1 to 500, or no whole number, is read as 50 rather than refused.

a page.summary: a page of the console's list

runId.name: id
runId.description: The run, by its identifier. One the caller may not read is answered as one that does not exist.

runStep.name: step
runStep.description: A step of the run, by the name the workflow file gives it.

runPort.name: port
runPort.description: A port of the step, by the name its brick declares.

error.summary: the port a brick sends what failed to

dispatchAttempt.name: attempt
dispatchAttempt.description: Which attempt's inputs, counted from 1 as AGK_ATTEMPT is. The last attempt dispatched where left out.

dispatchShard.name: shard
dispatchShard.description: Which shard's inputs, by the index AGK_SHARD carries before its slash. A step split into shards is asked about one of them; one that was not fanned out has none.

lastEventId.name: Last-Event-ID
lastEventId.description: The id of the last event a stream gave, <task_id>/<seq>/<line>, which a browser's EventSource sends by itself when it reconnects: the stream resumes after it, sending the dispatch_end it had sent last where it was cut between that and what follows.

outputName.name: name
outputName.description: A workflow output, by the name the workflow's outputs block gives it.

archived.summary: the output the archive step's port feeds

artifactUri.name: uri
artifactUri.description: The artifact's agk:// URI, as an envelope's file names it, percent-encoded as one path segment, so that a proxy in front passes %2F undecoded.

secret.name: name
secret.description: The secret's name, as the workflow file names it and as a step is given it at /agk/secrets/<name>: letters, digits, hyphens and underscores beginning with a letter or a digit, at most 255 characters.

variable.name: name
variable.description: The variable's name, read as vars.<name>: letters, digits, hyphens and underscores beginning with a letter or a digit, at most 255 characters, the grammar a workflow file's vars names its keys with.

avatarVersion.name: v
avatarVersion.description: Read by nobody: the avatar_updated_at of the user or the namespace whose picture it is, which a client writes here so that the picture's address changes when the picture does, and no cache answers a picture set again with the one before it.

set.summary: the instant the photo was set

pool.name: pool
pool.description: The runner pool, by its name, its only identity.

runner.name: runner
runner.description: The runner, by the identifier the API minted at its join.

auditLimit.name: limit
auditLimit.description: How many entries a page holds, from 1 to 200, 50 where it is left out: a screenful, and few enough that a page is answered at once.

auditBefore.name: before
auditBefore.description: The seq a page ends after: the entries before it, the newest first. Left out, the page starts at the last entry appended.

auditActor.name: actor
auditActor.description: The entries done by this principal, matched exactly.

auditAction.name: action
auditAction.description: The entries of this action, matched exactly.

auditNamespace.name: namespace
auditNamespace.description: The entries done in this namespace, matched exactly, and - for the acts on the installation, which name none.

auditTarget.name: target
auditTarget.description: The entries done to this target, matched exactly.

a run.summary: what was done to one run

auditSince.name: since
auditSince.description: The entries appended at this instant or after, in RFC 3339.

auditUntil.name: until
auditUntil.description: The entries appended at this instant or before, in RFC 3339.

setSession.description: The session cookie a sign-in opens: __Host-agentiik_session, HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax and Path=/, bound to no Domain and carrying no expiry of its own, so that the browser forgets it when it closes and the server ends it after 12 hours idle or 30 days at most. Its value is 256 bits, opaque, kept by the server as its SHA-256.

noStore.description: no-store, so that nothing on the way keeps a copy: on every answer carrying a secret shown once or what a sign-in opened, on every refusal, and on the sign-in page, which says what the installation offers when it is asked.

wwwAuthenticate.description: Bearer, on every 401: the scheme a request authenticates with besides the session cookie.

clearSession.description: The session cookie cleared: empty, and expired at once, with the attributes it was set with, so that the browser forgets it whether or not the server still knew the session.

noCache.description: no-cache: a browser may keep the file, and asks after it again at every load by its ETag, so that an upgrade never serves the page beside another release's scripts.

etag.description: The file's tag, drawn from its SHA-256, which a browser sends back in If-None-Match and is answered 304 for while the file is the same.

treeFileTag.description: With path, the file's SHA-256 in quotes: a file of a version is named by its content, so the same tag is the same bytes at whatever ref it is read. Absent from the listing.

pagePolicy.description: The Content-Security-Policy every answer of the sign-in page carries, its files' included: its own scripts, its own stylesheet and requests to its own origin, and nothing else. No form is posted, since a form posted from a page that sends no Referer carries Origin: null, which the API refuses; and the page is never framed, since a ceremony run in a frame is refused anyway and a page framed by another could be dressed to be clicked blind. Beside it, Referrer-Policy: no-referrer, since the page's address may carry agk login's challenge, and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, so that a file is only ever what its type says.

schema.const: default-src 'none'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; form-action 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'none'

policy.value: default-src 'none'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; form-action 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'none'

insufficientUserAuthentication.description: RFC 9470's challenge, on the refusal of a credential that lasts, asked from a session signed in to longer ago than 10 minutes, and on no other refusal: a client tells that one from the others by it rather than by the sentence, and the sign-in page then asks for a sign-in again, which opens a session whose opening is its proof.

sign in again.summary: a sign-in in the last 10 minutes asked for

retryAfter.description: The whole seconds until one more attempt fits in the sliding quarter of an hour, which the sign-in page turns into minutes for a person.

location.description: Where the workflow is read once the move is done: /api/v1/{target}/workflows/{name}.

privateDay.description: private, max-age=86400: the photo is kept a day by the browser that asked and by no shared cache, since it is shown to its owner and to administrators alone. A client asks for it at an address that changes with avatar_updated_at, so that keeping it a day never shows a photo set since.

noSniff.description: nosniff, so that a browser takes the body for the type it is declared as, and never for anything its bytes might be taken for.

avatarTag.description: The photo's tag, the instant it was set in microseconds since the epoch, in quotes, which a client keeping the photo past its day sends in If-None-Match and is answered 304 for while the photo is the same.

badRequest.description: The request is refused before it is read as one: a body that is not JSON, not UTF-8, holding a field the route does not read, a field written twice or anything after the document, or a value outside its grammar; a body sent to a route that reads none; or two credentials, a bearer token beside the session cookie or two session cookies, since a request is answered as one principal and which was meant is not the API's to guess.

unknown field.summary: a field the route does not read

value.error: the body holds a field this route does not read: kind
login: auth is reserved

two credentials.summary: a bearer token beside a session

value.error: this request carries more than one credential, a bearer token beside a session cookie or two session cookies, and a request is answered as one principal: send the one meant

unauthorised.description: No credential, or one that opens nothing: a bearer token this installation did not issue, revoked, expired or whose holder is suspended; or a session never opened here, signed out, revoked, idle 12 hours, 30 days old, its user suspended or removed, the credential that opened it removed, or, read from the policy at this request, a password's where passwords are now forbidden or a synced passkey's where device_bound_only now applies. One sentence for every reason of each, so that asking teaches nothing; once the bootstrap token has ended, a token's adds that it ended then, since the line left in .env is the likeliest token to stop working.

value.error: this request carries no credential
that token opens nothing: it is no API token this installation issued, or it was revoked or has expired, or its holder is suspended

that session opens nothing: it is no session this installation opened, or it was revoked, has ended or was left idle too long, or its holder is suspended. Sign in again, or open a fresh enrolment link

forbidden.description: The caller is known and may not do this: an administrator's route asked by somebody who does not administer the installation through the credential presented, a session that may only enrol anywhere but the routes it may reach, or a request changing something that a session carries from another origin than the public URL's.

not held.summary: a permission or a role not held

value.error: you do not hold what this needs

enrolment.summary: a session that may only enrol

value.error: this session enrols passkeys and nothing else

another origin.summary: a session carried from another page

value.error: a session changes something only from the pages of this installation's public URL, and this request's Origin header names another or none

notFound.description: Nothing there, or nothing the caller may see: the same answer for both, so that asking teaches nothing.

value.error: no such thing, or not yours

conflict.description: The request would leave a state the rules forbid.

value.error: finance is already a namespace
removing this passkey would leave fewer than min_passkeys

tooLarge.description: A body past 64 KiB, the cap the API's other small bodies carry, or holding more entries in a list than the route reads, 1,024 names at most: the request is larger than the route is willing to read, rather than wrong.

value.error: the body is larger than 64 KiB

unprocessable.description: The body is well formed and names something that is not there or not the caller's, or an instant outside what the route allows. One sentence for the absent and the hidden alike.

absent.summary: a principal that does not exist

value.error: principal group:team-nowhere names nobody
expires_at is more than a year away

signInAgain.description: The caller is known and may not do this. Where the reason is a session signed in to longer ago than 10 minutes, asked to add a credential that lasts, WWW-Authenticate carries RFC 9470's challenge, and the sign-in page asks for a sign-in again.

WWW-Authenticate.description: Present on the refusal for a sign-in older than 10 minutes, and on no other.

value.error: adding a way in takes a sign-in in the last 10 minutes, so that a session left open is not enough to add one, and this session was signed in to earlier: sign in again, then try once more

bearer token.summary: a credential set with a bearer token

value.error: a password and a TOTP generator are set and removed from a browser's session, on the sign-in page, and this request carries a bearer token: a token that leaked would otherwise be a way to a credential that outlives it

tooManyRequests.description: Too many password sign-ins tried in the last quarter of an hour: ten for the account from anywhere, or thirty from the address at any login, an IPv6 address counted by its /64. Answered before anything is read or hashed. Each replica of the API counts for itself, and a restart forgets.

value.error: too many password sign-ins were tried for this account or from this address in the last quarter of an hour: try again later, or sign in with a passkey

unavailable.description: The installation is checking too many passwords at once to check this one in time: a request that waits five seconds for its turn to hash is answered this, which says the installation is busy rather than that the password was wrong. A hash holds 19 MiB, so the API hashes one password per processor at once, within a quarter of its memory limit.

busy.summary: no turn to hash in time

value.error: this installation is checking too many passwords at once to check this one in time: try again in a moment
